current.text: Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, who all missed last season. He has to share the ball with them.
Experts agree he is unlikely to repeat last season's production with the new usage competition.
Josh expects him to start, but as only the fifth offensive option.
The fifth starter spot in Washington is not settled, with many wings competing for it.
Washington has a deep roster of wings. A 10 or 11 man rotation is expected, which spreads minutes.
Ben thinks he is the organization's favorite among its young wings and guards, and the best all-around player in that group.
If Anthony Davis is traded, Alex Sarr moves to center and George's starting role becomes secure, which helps him. One expert is about 80% sure Washington keeps Davis.
His ADP of 112 is marginally too high. One small forward ranking puts him in Tier 8.
Washington is trying to compete and aims for the play-in, so late-season resting and minutes cuts are not expected.

durable.text: Two-way wing who can guard shooting guard through power forward. He can struggle against quicker guards.
Shoots well from outside, especially on catch-and-shoot chances.
His blocks are clearly above average for a guard or forward.
An arm injury ended his 2025-26 season early.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both price him at 1 USD, with ranks of 121 and 129. Our league paid 2 USD last season. That puts him at the very end of a 144-player draft, and the experts see his ADP of 112 as a bit too high now that Young, Davis and Dybantsa take the touches. He has no flagged weak category and projects about 2.0 threes, 4.0 assists and 0.9 blocks, so he fits any build as a last-dollar pick. A projected 43% FG and 2.3 turnovers are the cost. Early in the season, check whether he holds the starting spot and his minutes stay near 29, and watch for an Anthony Davis trade, which would open a bigger role.
